Basque

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish patata, from Taíno batata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /patata/ [pa.t̪a.t̪a]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ata, -a
  • Hyphenation: pa‧ta‧ta

Noun

[edit]

patata inan

  1. potato

[edit]

Catalan

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pataca

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish patata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [pəˈta.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [paˈta.ta]
  • Audio (Valencia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ata
  • Hyphenation: pa‧ta‧ta

Noun

[edit]

patata f (plural patates)

  1. potato
    Synonyms: (Valencian) creïlla, (Northern) trumfa

Derived terms

[edit]
  • patata de Màlaga
  • patata fregida
  • patatada
  • patatar
  • patatera
  • truita de patates

Further reading

[edit]
  • “patata”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

[edit]

Borrowed from English potato.

patata m (plural patatys)

  1. potato
    Synonyms: aval dor, patatysen, tetti

Derived terms

[edit]
  • patata melys (“sweet potato”)

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish patata, from Taíno batata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [paˈtaː.ta]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [paˈtaː.ta]

Noun

[edit]

patāta f (genitive patātae); first declension

  1. (New Latin) potato
    Synonyms: solānum, colocāsia, malum terrae

Declension

[edit]

First-declension noun.

singular plural
nominative patāta patātae
genitive patātae patātārum
dative patātae patātīs
accusative patātam patātās
ablative patātā patātīs
vocative patāta patātae

Maltese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish patata, likely through Sicilian patata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /paˈtaː.ta/
  • Rhymes: -aːta

Noun

[edit]

patata f (collective, singulative patata, paucal patati)

  1. potato, potatoes
    Inħobb niekol il-patata. ― I like to eat potatoes.
    Kilt patata waħda biss. ― I only ate one potato.
    Għandna bżonn ħames patati. ― We need five potatoes.
    • 1932-1935, Melita agricola; rivista ta' cull xahar li tohrog mill-ufficciu tal-biedja, page 261:
      Il-patata titlob trab ħamri, u fejn jista’ jcun m’għandhiex tinżara’ fi trab ieħor.
      Potatoes need reddish soil, and as far as possible should not be planted in other kinds of soil.
  2. (slang) butt, backside, ass

Sardinian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish patata, from Taíno batata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /paˈtata/

Noun

[edit]

patata f (plural patatas)

  1. potato
    Synonym: pomu de terra

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Taíno batata. Compare batata. Though the Diccionario de la Real Academia Española lists it as a blend of papa +‎ batata.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /paˈtata/ [paˈt̪a.t̪a]
  • Audio (Spain):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ata
  • Syllabification: pa‧ta‧ta

Noun

[edit]

patata f (plural patatas)

  1. (Spain, Philippines) potato
    Synonym: (Hispanic America, Andalusia) papa
  2. (colloquial) piece of rubbish

Interjection

[edit]

¡patata!

  1. (Spain) cheese! Said while being photographed

Derived terms

[edit]
  • almidón de patata
  • comerse con patatas
  • donde no hay mata no hay patata
  • escarabajo de la patata
  • patata caliente
  • patata de caña
  • patata de Telinga
  • patata dulce
  • patatas alioli
  • patatas bravas
  • patatas fritas
  • patatero
  • pelapatatas
  • pisapatatas
  • tortilla de patata
  • tortilla de patatas

Further reading

[edit]
  • “patata”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
